newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end up, Albanian crisis seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end up, Albanian crisis seen easing.

text.p: Athens stocks closed 1.82 percent higher on moderate trading volume with analysts saying the general share index would rise this week on market expectations the Albanian crisis would start to improve.

"The market will rise in the short term as there is strong market belief that the crisis in Albania will be defused this week. Already, we saw a rise in Greek equities because of that on Monday," said analyst Pandelis Mytilinios, at Sarros Securities.
Albanian opposition politician Fatos Nano joined calls for Sali Berisha to quit following weeks of armed unrest in the Balkan country.
A European Union delegation was visiting Albania, on Monday to try and resolve the crisis.
Turnover had dropped as investors were cautious and waiting for further developments. A support level was around 1,200 to 1,250 by both Greek and foreign analysts, he said.
"On Monday, the market opened close to that level. It might have prompted some buying interest," he said.
The Athens general share index ended 1.82 percent or 23.14 points higher at 1291.28 points from Friday's 1268.14 after opening at 1267.45.
Turnover was 10.6 billion drachmas on volume of 2.9 million shares. Advancers led decliners 132 to 83 with 27 issues unchanged on 242 traded.
Leasing shares settled 8.0 percent higher and investment stocks gained 1.78 percent. Banks rose 2.74 percent, industrials closed 1.06 percent up and insurance gained 0.56 percent.
Construction stocks ended slightly lower, down 0.03 percent along with small caps, down 0.45 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 989.00-1027.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, gained 75 drachmas to settle at 5,850.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $41.14-$42.84. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 1,509-1,685 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 10,203-10,739 drachmas.
